newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: HK democracy leader to press Australia on China.
newsitem.headline: HK democracy leader to press Australia on China.

text.p: Hong Kong democracy campaigner Martin Lee said on Tuesday he would press Australian Prime Minister John Howard to take a tougher stand on China's adherence to international obligations towards Hong Kong.
Lee said he would hold an informal meeting with Howard on Thursday where he would discuss Beijing's plans to create a rival to Hong Kong's democratically-elected Legislative Council.
China's planned interim replacement for the council was in breach of the Sino-British agreement on Hong Kong's future after Beijing resumes control of the colony on July 1, 1997, Lee said.

"I will be telling your prime minister of the great importance of the leaders of the democratic countries to impress upon China that they are very interested indeed to keep Hong Kong as it is strictly under the one country, two systems policy," Lee told the National Press Club in Canberra.
"If China can be persuaded to keep her hands off, Hong Kong will continue to prosper," Lee said.
The informal meeting will take place at a cocktail party at the prime minister's official residence in Canberra after Lee reversed an earlier decision not to meet with Howard.
Howard refused a formal meeting with Lee, saying he was too busy. Lee said on Monday the refusal may have stemmed from Australian foreign ministry fears of upsetting Beijing.
Lee also warned that Asian business would suffer if China repressed Hong Kong as it could curtail the flow of accurate economic information because of media restrictions.
"Certainly on economic matters and political matters there is a certain degree, I have to say, of self-censorship already," Lee said. "You'll be making your commercial decisions blindfolded."

"So when the light goes out in Hong Kong, darkness doesn't fall just on Hong Kong, darkness doesn't just fall on China, it falls on the entire region and that is going to affect anyone investing in China."
